title: Proper base change on classical pro-étale complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of
schemes, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Set $X'=X\times_YY'$, with
projections $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$. If
$K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ has torsion underlying
abelian cohomology sheaves, the canonical exchange, defined as in
[sk-def-exchange] from the pro-étale inverse and direct images $g^*,g'^*$ and
$Rf_*,Rf'_*$ on $D^+(\,\cdot_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,

$$
g^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^*K
$$

is an isomorphism in $D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(Y'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

The complex $K$ need not be constructible, and the torsion orders need not be
invertible on $Y$. Classicality of $K$ is required: it is what brings the
statement back to the étale site.

proof.text:
Write $A_T=
u_T^*$. The bounded-below comparison unit is invertible, so the classical derived equivalence applies: $L=R
u_{X,*}K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and its counit $\alpha:A_XL\cong K$ is invertible because $K$ is classical. Exactness of the module comparison gives $A_XH^q(L)\cong H^q(K)$ for every $q$. Apply the torsion-reflection lemma to the exact fully faithful left adjoint $A_X$ (right adjoint $
u_{X,*}$): every $H^q(L)$ has torsion underlying abelian sheaf, with no uniform annihilator.

On abelian etale complexes put $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$, with the abelian derived exchange $\Ex:\Phi\to\Psi$. Abelian etale sheaves form Grothendieck categories and $f_*,f'_*$ are left exact additive, so the K-injective right derived direct images preserve every lower bound by negative vanishing; exact inverse images preserve cohomology. Both functors are triangulated and the exchange respects shifts. Torsion assembly makes it invertible on every $H^q(E)[0]$ when $E$ has torsion cohomology. The heart test therefore makes $\Ex_E$ invertible for every such $E\in D^+$.

Forgetting coefficients sends $L$ to an abelian complex with its underlying cohomology. The coefficient-forgetting comparison identifies the forgotten specified module exchange $e_L$ with the abelian exchange of step 2 and reflects invertibility. Hence $e_L$ is invertible.

The base change $f'$ is proper. Properness gives finite type and separatedness; finite type gives quasi-compactness, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. Apply discrete exchange site comparison: its canonical vertex isomorphisms satisfy $T_L A_{Y'}(e_L)=e^p_{A_XL}S_L$. Thus $e^p_{A_XL}=T_L A_{Y'}(e_L)S_L^{-1}$ is invertible, and both endpoints are bounded below and classical.

proof.text: Naturality of the ambient exchange along the counit isomorphism $\alpha:A_XL\cong K$ conjugates the preceding map to the exchange at $K$, and its two endpoint maps are isomorphisms. Hence its endpoints remain bounded below and classical. Their full derived subcategory contains the inverse, giving the claimed isomorphism.
